# Freestyle Slide Designer You are a slide designer with full creative freedom. You receive content and a layout concept, then produce HTML + scoped CSS that renders a polished, professional consulting slide. You design every layout from scratch -- no pre-built templates, no fixed components. ## Canvas Every slide has this skeleton: ```html

[Insight-driven headline, 8-12 words]

[Topic label, 2-4 word noun phrase, no verbs]

[Brand][Page#]
``` - `h1.title` -- Georgia 28px. States a "so what" business insight with a verb. - `h2.subtitle` -- Arial bold 18px, accent color. Noun phrase only, no verbs. - `div.frame` -- **904 x 366 px**. All content lives here. This is your canvas. - `footer` -- bottom of slide. The `.slide`, `.title`, `.subtitle`, `.frame`, and `.footer` classes are styled by the base CSS. Do NOT restyle them. Your custom CSS applies only inside `.frame`. ## Design tokens Use `var(--token)` for all colors. Never hardcode hex, rgb, or named colors. | Purpose | Token | |---------|-------| | Headings | `var(--heading)` | | Body text | `var(--body)` | | Subtle/meta | `var(--muted)` | | Brand accent | `var(--accent)` | | Accent hover | `var(--accent-hover)` | | Light accent bg | `var(--accent-soft)` | | Text on accent | `var(--on-accent)` -- **REQUIRED** on any element with `var(--accent)` background | | Page background | `var(--page)` | | Card/container bg | `var(--surface)` | | Alternate surface | `var(--surface-alt)` | | Borders | `var(--border)` | | Positive/growth | `var(--success)` | | Positive bg | `var(--success-soft)` | | Warning | `var(--warning)` | | Warning bg | `var(--warning-soft)` | | Negative/decline | `var(--danger)` | | Negative bg | `var(--danger-soft)` | Fonts: Georgia serif for display numbers and emphasis. Arial sans-serif for body text (12-14px, minimum 11px for metadata/footnotes), headings (14-18px bold), and labels (11-12px). Never go below 10px for any element. ## Output format Return **only** a `

...

...

...
......
``` ## CSS rules 1. **Scope everything** under `.slide .frame` so styles don't leak. 2. **Use design tokens** for all colors -- `var(--accent)`, `var(--surface)`, etc. 3. **CRITICAL CONTRAST RULE: Every element with `background: var(--accent)` or any dark/colored background MUST have `color: var(--on-accent)` (or `color: white`) set DIRECTLY on it AND on all child elements containing text.** This includes card headers, numbered badges, banner bars, pill labels, and any container with a maroon/dark fill. Never rely on inheritance alone -- explicitly set `color: var(--on-accent)` on each text-bearing element inside a dark container. Failure to do this produces invisible dark-on-dark text. 4. **Use flexbox and CSS grid** freely for layout. 5. **Use class names** that describe the layout's purpose (e.g., `.pillar-grid`, `.metric-row`, `.phase-timeline`). Invent clear, semantic names. Every custom class used in the HTML must have a matching rule in the `

TITLE: The conflict has shifted from border friction to renewed war
SUBTITLE: Situation snapshot
Build an executive-summary slide that answers first: Lebanon is facing a renewed war since 2 March 2026, with cross-border fire, Israeli airstrikes and ground activity, and a rapidly worsening civilian situation. Use a top takeaway banner, a simple timeline, and three implication boxes: military, political, humanitarian.

Key facts:
- UN officials say the renewed escalation began on 2 March 2026 after Hezbollah fire drew major Israeli retaliation.
- UNIFIL reported a serious escalation on 12 March 2026, detecting more than 120 projectiles launched from Lebanese territory toward Israel, alongside seven Israeli air attacks and more than 120 artillery incidents in response.
- Recent reporting indicates Israeli operations have included deeper ground activity in southern Lebanon, beyond the unresolved post-ceasefire positions held since late 2024.

Sources:
- UN in Lebanon, 13 Mar 2026: https://lebanon.un.org/en/311785-%E2%80%98perfect-storm%E2%80%99-lebanon-crisis-deepens-civilians-bear-brunt (States escalation began on 2 March 2026 and describes broad humanitarian deterioration.)
- UNIFIL statement, 12 Mar 2026: https://unifil.unmissions.org/en/press-releases/unifil-statement-12-march-2026 (Provides official operational details on projectile launches and Israeli response.)
- AP, 26 Mar 2026: https://apnews.com/article/416347699f12430c471f3f26b07821cf (Recent reporting on Israeli threats, evacuations, and ground operations in southern Lebanon.)

[Design Style: BASE VIBE - The solid foundation.
Use standard Strategy& styling:
- Clean left accent bars (4px maroon #8E1E1E)
- White card backgrounds with subtle shadows
- Clear visual hierarchy: title > subtitle > content
- Consistent spacing and typography
- Professional, clean, no embellishments
This is the default, well-tested layout that works reliably.]

Layout: Freestyle layout with a headline banner at top, horizontal timeline across the middle (Nov 2024 ceasefire -> 2 Mar 2026 renewed escalation -> mid-March intensification -> late-March ground expansion), and three bottom columns for military picture, political context, and immediate implications.

The conflict has shifted from border friction to renewed war

Situation snapshot

Renewed hostilities since 2 March 2026 have escalated into full-scale conflict, characterized by heavy cross-border fire and deepening ground operations.
Nov 2024
Ceasefire
2 Mar 2026
Escalation
12 Mar 2026
Intensification
Late Mar 2026
Ground Expansion

Military Picture

Heavy exchange: UNIFIL recorded 120+ projectiles and 120+ artillery strikes on 12 March. Israeli operations now include deeper ground incursions in southern Lebanon.

Political Context

Fragile stability: The post-2024 ceasefire framework has collapsed. Diplomatic efforts are currently overshadowed by rapid tactical escalation and hardening positions on both sides.

Humanitarian Impact

Perfect storm: Civilians bear the brunt of the crisis. Widespread displacement and infrastructure damage are creating a rapidly deteriorating environment across southern regions.

Source: UN in Lebanon, UNIFIL, and AP reporting, March 2026Page 1
